title: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan Enables Integrated and Coordinated Infrastructure Planning
subtitle: PM GatiShakti Provides Integrated Planning Framework without Separate Budgetary Provisions
body_text:
PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (PMGS NMP), launched in October 2021, is a transformative “Whole of Government” approach to bring together various Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs to ensure integrated planning and coordinated execution of infrastructure projects. PMGS NMP aims to facilitate Ministries/States in data driven decision making by utilizing geospatial data, satellite imagery and API integration to monitor, plan, and optimize infrastructure development. The PMGS NMP is facilitating Ministries/States in planning of their respective infrastructure projects, including social infrastructure projects, in integrated, synchronized and coordinated manner to provide seamless and efficient connectivity for the movement of people, goods, and services across various modes of transport, thereby enhancing last-mile connectivity and reducing travel time.
PM GatiShakti provides an integrated planning framework; the approval and implementation of the projects are undertaken by the respective central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs under their plans, schemes, procedures and budgetary/funding provisions. Hence, no quantified targets or expenditure requirements have been set under PM GatiShakti initiative.
The Network Planning Group (NPG), constituted under the PM GatiShakti framework, evaluates the critical infrastructure projects of the central Government to ensure integrated planning, multimodality, inter-modality, synchronization of efforts, last mile connectivity, comprehensive development in and around the project location, data driven decision makings, etc at the planning stage. As on date, 396 infrastructure projects with total estimated cost of about ₹ 18.66 Lakh Crore have been evaluated through the NPG mechanism. Out of these 396 projects, 256 projects have been sanctioned - out of which, 198 projects are under implementation. Ministry-wise details are given at Annexure-A.
Government carries out assessment of its initiatives/schemes from time to time through various studies, surveys, etc. Apart from these, there are several studies by universities and research scholars in this respect. As per these assessments, the integrated planning initiatives like, PM GatiShakti, National Logistics Policy, PRAGATI, Sagarmala, development of connectivity infrastructure (expressways/ national highways/ dedicated rail freight corridors and rail tracks, industrial corridors/hubs), etc. have shaped the vision of connected and competitive India and have improved logistics efficiency, turn-around time, ease of doing business, industrial growth and reduced logistics cost in country. An assessment of logistic cost has been carried out by DPIIT in the year 2025 in collaboration with National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER). As per the assessment, the logistics cost in India is estimated at 7.9% of the GDP, which is at par with the advanced economies in the world. The Economic Survey 2023-24 highlighted that these measures have improved domestic manufacturing and export competitiveness. A study by Indian Institute of Management, Bangalore on impact of development of National Highway projects underlines that every-one rupee expenditure in National Highways development leads to a ₹3.2 increase in Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
So far 58 Central Ministries/Departments and all 36 States/UTs have been onboarded on the PMGS NMP, covering all infrastructure sectors like road, rail, ports & waterways, power, petroleum & natural gas, civil aviation, telecommunications, industrial corridors, etc. Further, PM GatiShakti public platform (url: ugi.pmgatishakti.gov.in) has been launched in September 2025, which provided access of PM GatiShakti data analytics to private entities and general public. Through this Query based mechanism, public and private entities are able to plan their projects by obtaining data analytic reports from the PMGS-NMP Portal through a simple query-based mechanism. The States have been encouraged to expand the use of PM GatiShakti for district level planning. About 1800 data layers have been integrated and over 65 software modules/tools and more than 100 mobile/web applications have been developed and integrated on the platform for the use of stakeholders. Further expansion of the PM GatiShakti initiative is a continuous process - mapping/integration of more data layers, development and integration of additional features, software modules/tools for planning and analysis modules/tools, mobile/ web applications, etc. to be continue further as per the requirements of the Ministries/Departments, States/UTs and other stakeholders.
This information was given by Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Jitin Prasada in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Commerce & Industry informed Lok Sabha that PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (PMGS NMP), launched in October 2021, has evaluated 396 infrastructure projects worth about ₹18.66 lakh crore through its Network Planning Group, of which 256 are sanctioned and 198 under implementation. All 58 central Ministries/Departments and 36 States/UTs have been onboarded, and a public platform (ugi.pmgatishakti.gov.in) launched in September 2025 gives private entities and citizens access to data analytics. A DPIIT-NCAER 2025 study estimated India's logistics cost at 7.9% of GDP, comparable to advanced economies.
enrichment.context:
PM GatiShakti is a 'Whole of Government' digital platform integrating geospatial and satellite data from multiple ministries to enable synchronized planning of infrastructure across roads, railways, ports, aviation, power, and industrial corridors, aiming to reduce logistics costs and improve last-mile connectivity. It complements the National Logistics Policy (2022), Sagarmala, Bharatmala, and industrial corridor projects, and is central to India's push to lower logistics costs (historically estimated at 13-14% of GDP) to levels competitive with advanced economies (8-9%), which affects export competitiveness, manufacturing (Make in India, PLI schemes) and ease of doing business rankings. Since PM GatiShakti is a planning and coordination framework rather than a funding scheme, actual project approval, implementation and budgetary allocation remain with the concerned ministries/states, which distinguishes it from typical centrally-sponsored schemes with dedicated financial outlays.

The Network Planning Group (NPG) mechanism institutionalizes multi-modal integration at the appraisal stage itself, addressing India's historical problem of infrastructure silos (e.g., roads built without utility ducts, ports lacking rail linkages). The mention of the IIM-Bangalore finding that ₹1 spent on highways yields ₹3.2 GDP growth underscores the multiplier effect rationale behind infrastructure-led growth strategy, a theme recurring in Economic Surveys and Budget speeches.

prelims_questions.question:
With reference to PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in October 2021.
2. It provides separate budgetary allocations for infrastructure projects sanctioned under it.
3. All 36 States/UTs have been onboarded on the platform.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: PM GatiShakti was launched in October 2021 and all 36 States/UTs have been onboarded, but it is an integrated planning framework without separate budgetary provisions; funding remains with respective ministries/states under their own schemes.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Network Planning Group (NPG)', mentioned in the context of PM GatiShakti, is primarily concerned with which of the following?
options: Disbursing funds for infrastructure projects to states
Evaluating central infrastructure projects for integrated, multimodal planning at the appraisal stage
Monitoring cybersecurity of government digital platforms
prelims_questions.explanation: NPG evaluates critical central government infrastructure projects to ensure integrated planning, multimodality, last-mile connectivity and synchronization at the planning stage, not fund disbursement or telecom regulation.

mains_questions.question: PM GatiShakti has been described as a 'Whole of Government' approach to infrastructure planning. Discuss how such integrated planning frameworks help overcome the traditional silos in India's infrastructure development, and examine the challenges in their effective implementation.

Examine the role of logistics efficiency in enhancing India's manufacturing and export competitiveness. In this context, discuss the significance of reducing logistics costs as a percentage of GDP and the initiatives undertaken to achieve this.
